row.question:
Based on Figure 5, which of the following findings would indicate a possible recurrence of ganglioneuroblastoma in the right subclavicular fossa?  
A) Presence of a new paravertebral mass with calcifications  
B) Clear lung fields with no new mass  
C) Increased pleural effusion on the right side  
D) Right-sided costal excision with no mass  
E) New mass in the left subclavicular fossa  
F) Diffuse bilateral lung infiltrates

reference.correct_choice_text: Presence of a new paravertebral mass with calcifications

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When mediastinal opacity obscures one heart border and tracheal deviation is present on PA CXR
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect which cardiac border is silhouetted (left border loss = left mediastinal pathology; right border loss = right-sided) and confirm tracheal deviation direction—deviation away from mass side—and compare costophrenic angle blunting severity per side.
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable if both borders obscured or in severe cardiomegaly; requires adequate inspiration and centering.

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When PA CXR shows enlarged central pulmonary arteries and cardiomegaly with right heart border prominence, and symptoms suggest chronic dyspnea
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect lateral CXR for convex retrosternal clear space and posterior displacement of heart—signs of right ventricular hypertrophy—and exclude left-sided volume overload signs (e.g., upper lobe vessel redistribution, Kerley B lines)
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable in poor inspiration or scoliosis; does not differentiate etiology of PH (e.g., sarcoid vs. IPAH)
